title: Perfect Chemistry
author: Simone Elkeles
current_text: In 2017, a parent challenged Perfect Chemistry at Academy School District 20’s Challenger Middle School Library, objecting to language, alcohol use, violence and sexual descriptions; after an appeal to the school board, the superintendent’s office overturned its previous decision and pulled the book and the series. The school board voted to ban Perfect Chemistry from the Challenger Middle School Library in Colorado, upholding a ruling that it was not age-appropriate for a middle school audience because of descriptions of sexual encounters, drug and alcohol use, violence and profanity.

sources.quote: A parent challenged the book, objecting to language, alcohol use, violence and sexual descriptions. I had a chance to talk to Gina T. Schaarschmidt, the Challenger Middle School librarian, about the challenge and her experience working with the Office for Intellectual Freedom.
sources.title: Defending Books in a Middle School: an Interview with Librarian Gina Schaarschmidt - Intellectual Freedom Blog

sources.quote:
D-20 board members said the issue is not one of freedom of speech, but rather doing their job to not expose young students to unsuitable adult topics.

Board members unanimously agreed at a July 20 meeting to uphold a superintendent designee’s ruling that the book is “not age-appropriate for a middle school audience because of pervasive descriptions of graphic sexual encounters, drug/alcohol use, violence and use of profanity.”
sources.title: Book banning in Academy School District 20: Censorship or diligence? - The Gazette

sources.quote: Banned from the Challenger Middle School Library (Colorado) when administration overruled a review committee that had unanimously recommended to retain Perfect Chemistry.

The book review committee, librarians, educators, and parents filed a 92-page appeal to the school board in hopes of overturning the superintendent’s censorship of the book. The school board voted to ban the book.
